name: Garden for the Environment
description: A public teaching garden with compost, food, and native-plant demonstration areas plus hands-on gardening workshops.
access: Sign up for an open volunteer shift or a workshop, or walk the self-guided garden tour. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
sourcePublisher: Garden for the Environment (Earth Island Institute)
evidence: We are a public teaching garden in San Francisco offering collaborative, hands-on, skilled, and hopeful programming

name: Candlestick Point Native Plant Nursery (Literacy for Environmental Justice)
description: A youth-staffed nursery that grows local native plants for habitat restoration in San Francisco parks and open spaces.
access: Come to a standing nursery volunteer day or arrange a group workday through LEJ; some restoration events have a minimum age. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: The nursery employs local teens and engages the community in the process of growing plants, restoring local habitats

name: Quesada Gardens
description: Neighbors turned a neglected street median into a vegetable and flower garden that volunteers still tend together.
access: Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the site to join neighbors caring for the median garden. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: the entire length of the median was transformed from weeds, garbage, and neglect into a bountiful vegetable and flower garden.

name: Ecology Center
description: A Berkeley nonprofit with a resource center, library, and classes on healthy food systems, zero waste, and climate action.
access: Visit the store and environmental resource center during open hours, or apply to volunteer with the farmers' market or other programs. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: We provide information, educational opportunities, tools, and products to assist and develop your sustainable lifestyle.

name: Ardenwood Historic Farm
description: A working regional-park farm where families help plant, tend, and harvest organic crops and learn farm history.
access: Visit during park hours (entry fee) and join public naturalist programs, or ask about volunteering as a farm demonstrator. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Public non-reservation weekend programs include the planting, tending, and harvesting of Ardenwood's organic crops

name: Alameda Point Collaborative Farm2Market
description: An urban farm and plant nursery inside a supportive-housing community, where volunteers weed, plant, and propagate.
access: Fill out the volunteer form to help as an urban farmer or nursery volunteer; group projects ask for a donation. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Volunteer as an Urban Farmer to help contribute to the successful operations of our farm and the APC community.

name: Unity Park Edible Forest (Urban Tilth)
description: An edible forest of 80+ fruit trees and free-harvest garden beds along the Richmond Greenway, cared for by Urban Tilth.
access: Pick fruit and join volunteer days or garden workshops on the Greenway; contact Urban Tilth to plan a group project. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Explore our incredible Edible Forest, a thriving multi-layered ecosystem boasting over 80 fruit trees, including cherries, apples, pears, and more.

name: The Gardens at Heather Farm
description: A free six-acre public garden with demonstration and children's gardens, plant propagation, and youth nature classes.
access: Walk the garden for free, or apply to join weekday garden-maintenance or plant-propagation volunteer crews. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Kids can learn about wildlife habitats, geology, plant anatomy, water conservation, environmental stewardship, and more.

name: Markham Nature Park and Arboretum
description: A 17-acre volunteer-run nature park with an arboretum, tree walks, and a community garden growing food and pollinator plants.
access: Explore the park and tree walk, or contact the society about volunteer garden work; training is provided. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: an active Community Garden growing edible plants and pollinators year 'round.

name: Slide Ranch
description: A coastal teaching ranch where kids milk goats, collect eggs, and cook food from the garden.
access: Register for a monthly volunteer day or a family farm program; youth under 14 come with a participating adult. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: They milk goats, collect eggs, and cook farm-fresh food from the garden.

name: Occidental Arts & Ecology Center
description: An 80-acre permaculture demonstration site with organic gardens, orchards, and an organic perennial plant nursery.
access: Drop in for a seasonal guided tour or a weekly garden volunteer day (volunteers must be 16+), or shop the nursery. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Our Saturday tours showcase our organic gardens and orchards, ecological design demonstration site, and programs.

name: Cavanagh Center Food Forest (Daily Acts)
description: One of Daily Acts' public demonstration gardens, showing food forests, water-wise natives, and rain-capture ideas.
access: Stroll the garden anytime it is open, or sign up for a Garden Steward workday or planting day on the Daily Acts site. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: planting a food forest, installing and maintaining drip irrigation systems, pruning woody perennials and fruit or native trees, building rain gardens

name: Sonoma Garden Park (Sonoma Ecology Center)
description: A 6.1-acre public garden with sustainable food gardens, chickens, a harvest market, and a native plant nursery.
access: Drop in during posted volunteer hours to help in the gardens or native nursery, or visit the park and nursery. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Sonoma Garden Park is a 6.1 acre public garden located at 19996 7th St E in Sonoma and is open daily from sunrise to sunset.

name: Connolly Ranch Education Center
description: A historic farm where kids learn in an edible garden, care for heritage animals, and explore oak woodland trails.
access: Register for a family program or Sunday Farm Open House, or apply as a garden or animal-care volunteer. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: We care for numerous fruit trees, perennials and California native flora to foster a pollinator friendly environment.

name: Rush Ranch
description: A protected ranch and tidal-marsh reserve with native grasslands, trails, and hands-on ranching-history demonstrations.
access: Hike the trails, come to a Get the Rush family day, or join Solano Land Trust's monthly volunteer workday. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
address: 3521 Grizzly Island Road, Suisun City, CA 94585
evidence: Designated as a National Estuarine Research Reserve, Rush Ranch supports critical research on marsh ecosystems, serves as a hub for community education

name: Avant Garden (Benicia Community Gardens, Sustainable Solano)
description: An organic community garden with an outdoor education area and a share plot where volunteers grow food to donate.
access: Join a monthly community garden or share-plot workday, or fill out Sustainable Solano's volunteer form. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: there are 43 garden beds, a shed, an outdoor education area, a picnic area, and our beloved " Benicia Community Share " plot

name: Pie Ranch
description: A coastal farm focused on food education and regenerative agriculture, with a native garden and monthly community workdays.
access: Pre-register for a weekly or monthly farm volunteer shift or a restoration day at a neighboring ranch. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Every 3rd Saturday, the workday begins at 3 pm in the Native Garden behind Pie Ranch's Roadside Barn, located at 2080 Cabrillo Hwy, Pescadero.

name: Filoli Historic House & Garden
description: A historic estate garden that composts on site, uses drip irrigation, and is adding native and drought-tolerant plants.
access: Buy a timed ticket to tour the garden, orchard, and trails, or join a guided garden program. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: Increased use of native and drought-tolerant plants to reduce water dependence.

name: Hidden Villa
description: A ranch with a small organic farm, education gardens, and trails offering hands-on farm and nature programs.
access: Visit the education garden and trails, or sign up for a farm volunteer shift or family program on the program calendar. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
address: 26870 Moody Road, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022
evidence: Hidden Villa manages a small-scale, organic farm that teaches about and produces responsible food.

name: Veggielution Community Farm
description: An East San José urban farm where neighbors farm together, explore a youth garden, and shop produce grown on site.
access: Come to the monthly First Saturday open house to volunteer in the fields, tour the farm, or take a class. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
address: 647 S. King Road, San José, CA 95116
evidence: Every first Saturday of the month, over 100 neighbors join us to farm, make new friends, and shop our Farm Stand

name: Our City Forest Community Nursery & Training Center
description: A community nursery growing native and drought-tolerant trees and shrubs for planting, with workshops on tree care.
access: Visit during nursery hours or register on Eventbrite for a nursery workday or neighborhood tree planting. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: All our plants are available on a tax-deductible donation basis, and visitors can attend workshops on planting, care and propagation.

name: Deer Hollow Farm
description: A free working homestead farm inside an open space preserve, with farm animals and a volunteer-tended garden and orchard.
access: Walk in from the park lots during farm hours, or apply to volunteer (ages 14+, with application and background check). Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
evidence: You can also enjoy friendly farm animals, as well as a garden and orchard supported by volunteers, during regular farm hours.

name: UCSC Farm & Alan Chadwick Garden (Center for Agroecology)
description: Certified-organic campus farm and garden used to teach and research organic growing, open free to visitors.
access: Take a free self-guided visit during open hours, or fill out the volunteer interest form for work days and events. Confirm current schedule and age requirements with the team.
sourcePublisher: UC Santa Cruz Center for Agroecology
evidence: These sites are both open to the public from 8am to 6pm daily, with no admission fees.
